summary: The Wizard steps on a teleport trap while magic resistant. C teleport.c:tele_trap calls display.c:shieldeff, then reports a wrenching sensation without moving the hero. JavaScript preflight refuses this branch because shieldeff is unported. Port the complete display.c helper, then admit the existing teleport.c branch and preserve its guard and effect order.

source.branch: teleport.c:tele_trap (1492-1535) takes Antimagic before displacement, calls display.c:shieldeff(u.ux,u.uy), and prints a wrenching sensation. display.c:shieldeff (1110-1123) checks flags.sparkle and cansee, displays SHIELD_COUNT source glyphs with flush/delay, then restores newsym.
callers: hack.c:spoteffects -> trap.c:dotrap -> trapeffect_telep_trap(hero) -> teleport.c:tele_trap -> display.c:shieldeff when Antimagic; the JS path is refused by js/trap_effects.js:preflight_dotrap before game state changes.

Other active C shieldeff callers are trap.c:trapeffect_fire_trap(monster), trap.c:trapeffect_anti_magic, trap.c:dofiretrap, and trap.c:chest_trap; wire the display helper to source paths as each is ported.
dependencies: Use source SHIELD_COUNT/shield_static glyph sequence, show_glyph, flush_screen(1), nh_delay_output, newsym, flags.sparkle, and cansee in the same order; this impure helper needs complete recorded-play evidence.

js/teleport.js:tele_trap already has the Antimagic and recursive-entry guard but throws in the shieldeff branch; js/trap_effects.js preflight rejects this case before teleport dispatch. Remove the refusal only when the complete effect can run.
The v11 recording name describes a hoped-for displacement, but this Wizard is magic resistant and the C source outcome is a wrenching sensation; preserve C behavior rather than the case label.
